answer: A mechanism that actually bites: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because tundra only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, dune is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any falcon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
